NLP / TRANSFORMERS

Automatic Meeting Summarizer

I wanted a faster way to revisit the main points from a meeting. I built a Flask app that turns a pasted transcript into a short recap.

PythonPyTorchTransformersFlaskPegasus
Explore the repository ↗
Problem

Why this project?

A transcript is useful when you need the exact wording. I wanted to see how well an abstractive summarizer could help someone find the main points before returning to the full conversation.

Approach

From input to output.

I explored T5, LED, BART, and Pegasus in separate fine-tuning notebooks. I connected the fine-tuned Pegasus model to a Flask interface that sends transcript text to the model and returns a generated summary.

A simplified overview of the repository’s application flow.

Implementation
01

Model exploration

Separate notebooks support experimentation with four transformer architectures for summarization.

02

Web interface

A Flask endpoint receives transcript text and returns the generated summary as JSON.

03

Inference pipeline

The application uses PyTorch, selects CUDA when available, and applies generation settings to control length and repetition.

What I learned and what to keep in mind

The app takes up to 512 input tokens, so a long transcript can lose later discussion before summarization begins. That limit shaped what I would test next: whether splitting a long transcript preserves decisions from across the meeting. The app requires local fine-tuned model files, and important details in the output should be checked against the transcript.
